rubric_notes: Correct hierarchy and all families with sunids supported by bundle; HU/IHF correctly placed in a.55.1.1 'Prokaryotic DNA-bending protein' (supported by DNA-bending search). Superfamily = probable common origin inferred from structure; family = sequence-detectable. Explicit limit that function should not be transferred across families (TAF/NC2/NF-Y/Sos heterodimerization modules; bacterial members uncharacterized) and that automated matches are uncurated. Linker histones and modifying enzymes correctly excluded. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4, shared superfamily a.204.1 with correct sunids (113676, 122676, 116993, 140797, 101386) matching the bundle; sibling dUTPase family supported by search results. Clearly distinguishes fold vs superfamily vs family semantics, states probable common ancestry at superfamily level only, rejects HisE/MazG substrate and pathway transfer in both directions, notes hypothetical-protein status of SSo12199, and lists external evidence needed. No material errors.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, sunids, duplication comment, and complete sibling-family list supported by bundle. Gives the remote-homology inference with conserved phosphate/adenosine motifs and ATP-binding architecture, explicitly names unsafe transfers (sugar-kinase activity to actin/HSP70, polymerization/chaperone behaviour to kinases, ligand-specificity and allosteric residues), notes functional breadth across sibling families, fold-level neighbours share only topology, and template/representative limits. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Meets must_include: three families under a.25.1 with supported sunids, superfamily as probable common ancestry via conserved metal-ligand motifs, chemistry divergence, external evidence (ligand conservation, EPR/spectroscopy, assays) named. However, describes a.25.2-a.25.6 as 'unrelated-by-descent' superfamilies, asserting nonhomology from superfamily separation alone, which SCOPe does not assert. Minor descriptive imprecision calling the a.25 fold 'up-and-down' despite the crossover connection. Classification identifiers correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily, protein-node sunids and domains (d1ikop_, d2hleb_, d2dexx2, d3b1ua1) matching bundle; b.6.2 correctly described as fold-only. Remote homology stated at superfamily strength, copper/ET transfer refused as family-level property, required external evidence given. Loose wording calling automated-match protein nodes 190316/190545 'families' is not material. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, sunids, Pfam xrefs, sibling families, 15 fold superfamilies and automated-match protein sunids (190118, 191298, 190541) all supported by bundle. Superfamily correctly framed as probable common origin of a beta-grasp interaction scaffold, a scaffold-level not function-level grouping; fold-level sharing implies no homology claim. Explicitly rejects transfer of modifier/conjugation, GTPase binding, p97 binding, binding surfaces, within-RBD specificity, within-d.15.1.1 modifier status, interface templates, and Pfam beyond family; names required external evidence. Minor unverifiable SUMO-3/Ubl5 only.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, species, domain ids and the '25 named proteins plus automated matches' count match the bundle, and the biological reasoning is complete (superfamily homology vs fold, pseudo-receiver KaiA, non-catalytic wing, no cross-family transfer of signaling/catalysis/clock function, narrow sampling caveat). However it asserts the KaiA C-terminal domain is 'a.172.1 in SCOPe'; the actual placement is a.186.1.1, and this SCCS was not retrieved. Fabricated release-specific classification triggers the factual_support ceiling of 1.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Verified b.84.5 (310577), b.84.5.1 (310616), two protein entries with correct structures (3a5c/3gqb/9u6x, 3j9t; 1vdz, 3ikj), five siblings with comments, PubMed xref (Numoto et al. 2009 correct). Correctly describes the bulge as an insertion making the c.37.1.11 domain discontinuous. Evolutionary claims stated at correct strength: fold-level only toward b.84.1-b.84.4 with remote divergence or convergence left open, family-level homology among V1/A1 bulges, and excision as an independent domain. Rejects cross-superfamily function/binding-site transfer and sequence-level template use; notes curatorial boundary could be revised. 1vdz/3a5c domain-layout details not in bundle but plausible and uncontradicted.

Correct three-superfamily structure with sunids and families; correctly explains fold vs superfamily vs family assertions; cites 'possible link' comment as hypothesis not merger; rejects cross-superfamily function/template transfer; lists external evidence. Mention of cytochrome b6 and d1siwc_ is accurate SCOPe content though not in its bundle. No material errors.

Identifiers, lineage, 13-family count, sole-superfamily status of fold c.2 and release metadata all supported by the bundle. Correctly distinguishes family (close homology, not shared), superfamily (probable common origin, remote homology, functionally diverged) and fold/class (no evolutionary claim), and explicitly refuses to infer dehydrogenase activity for RCK domains, alcohol oxidation for CoA-binding domains, or channel gating for ADH domains; notes ligand identity is not guaranteed across families. Lists required external evidence and the automated-match caveat. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct identifiers and same-family placement (k.40.1.1, sunid 100905); class k reasoning sound; 'Unnamed design-2' sibling supported by search bundle. Never retrieved or mentions the family's 'not a true family' curator comment (states no comment text was returned), so the decisive annotation is ignored; bio ceiling <=2. Minor unverified release date detail not penalized. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Must_include met: 1.69 c.137/c.137.1/c.137.1.1 verified via resolve, with correct d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ whole-chain domains vs 1f8y c.23.14.1 under superfamily then named N-deoxyribosyltransferase (verified); 2.08 c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 under renamed c.23.14 (verified); 1.71/1.73 c.23.14.2 verified so move dated to 1.71. Frames the change as upgrading from unrelated folds to probable common ancestry at superfamily strength, explicitly separating the later tag-split boundary refinement. Correct d1t1ja1 as current SID and warns against mixing release-specific sccs. Caveats on function transfer, fold-level non-homology, and template use present. Claim that the decision 'has not been re-curated since' is unverifiable but non-material.

Correct identification of d1a14h2 as the l.1.1.1 synthetic N-terminal tag with full lineage and sunids (supported), d1a14h1 as b.1.1.1 VH H:9-111, and clear rejection of tag similarity as homology with explanation that class l levels carry no evolutionary meaning. Release dates supported by its releases response. Minor unverified generalities (ASTRAL exclusion, 1.75-era handling) are plausible and not release-specific fabrications.

Accurate 1.75 whole-chain classification, accurate 2.04-onward split with correct sunids and boundaries, and correct lineages for both current domains. Module interpretation is well grounded in the multi-family PA14-like superfamily and the retrieved Pfam cross-reference, and the asymmetry against the singleton C-terminal lineage is stated. Adds a useful fragment caveat about short PA14 regions in other entries, keeps fold-level matches non-homologous, and requires external profile or structural evidence before transfer.

All five domains correctly identified with SIDs, boundaries and sccs (d3jb9a5 A:47-697 d.394.1.1 new fold; a4 bromodomain a.29.2.1; a3 e.8.1.8; a2 c.52.1.36; a1 c.55.3.14). Mosaic interpretation with reused modules vs. innovation, family vs superfamily distinction, group II intron inference flagged as inference, explicit refusal to transfer catalytic/acetyl-lysine function, FATCAT/AlphaFold singleton evidence supported by bundle. Jab1/MPN omission and cryo-EM caveats stated. Minor unverified extras (5qy*/5r0* fragment-screen entries) not supported by bundle but noncentral.

Correct shared family a.298.1.1 with lineage sunids and the three protein/species nodes, and the copy-number explanation plus unsafe-transfer and template limits are well argued. Decisive omission: never cites the 're' heterogeneity code or the canonical representative repeat unit (4cj9 A:259-292, representative d4cj9a_), which is the annotation that licenses unequal lengths within one family; this triggers the repeat-annotation ceiling. Invents SCOPe/PDB annotation text ('keyworded 1.5 repeat units', 'keyworded 11 tandem repeats') and an unsupported 33-residue BurrH repeat with 19-20 copies, none of which appear in its evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All metadata matches evidence bundle. Cites stable 2.08 as frozen snapshot; preserves exact dated periodic label when depending on update-only domains; explains periodic label as stable version plus date representing incremental automated additions without restructuring the hierarchy. No must_avoid violations.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Places d1br0a_, d1ez3a/b/c_ and d1dn1b_ in a.47.2.1 (bundle-supported), documents the 2.08 'ms' flag vs 1.75 comment-only, the 1dn1 obsolescence and automated match to d3c98b_, and correctly reads the fragments' a.47 label as inherited from the complete four-helix domain rather than demonstrated by the three-helix Habc coordinates; spectrin resemblance kept at fold/analogy level; function-transfer and external-evidence limits stated. Noncentral error: SNARE fusion complex given as h.1.2 (SCOPe uses h.1.15.1). Some release-history claims (2.01-2.05 absence, obsolete date) are true but not in this bundle.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Gives convergence vs divergence, level semantics, good reasons why cofactor sites converge, and an evidence-integration list. But asserts non-homology from fold difference ('shared cofactor without shared fold is, by definition, not homology') and calls c.3/d.58/c.4/c.1/c.31 cases convergent without the caveat that separate placement is not proof of independent origin. Factual error: describes fold c.4 as 'dihydrofolate reductase-like/transhydrogenase' (DHFR is c.71; transhydrogenase dIII is c.31.1.4; c.4.1 holds adrenodoxin reductase and D-amino acid oxidase N-terminal domains). Evidence bundle is thin (search only); c.2, c.3, d.58.20 identifiers are supported.

Correct and detailed on both release states, the dissolution of b.23.2 and b.23.2.1, the new family b.18.1.36 under superfamily b.18.1, the unchanged b.18.1.3 placement, the 2.05 timing and the separate 2.06 boundary change, with independent family members from 1nqj. Reasoning is strong: superfamily means probable not demonstrated ancestry, families are deliberately kept apart, no ligand, catalytic or template transfer, representative-selection and release-pinning caveats, and a clear list of external evidence needed. Deduction because key structural and functional support is presented from recalled literature rather than retrieved records, it does not cite the curated PubMed 17977833 family note that its own search of the hierarchy would have supplied, and it quotes a 2.04 freeze date not present in its bundle.

Bundle supports lineage, Pfam PF00046 at family node, sequences, hf record, fatcat-chain-statistics and AlphaFold matches. Correctly notes NHE is a heterogen not DNA, derives L16A/K52E from SEQRES, keeps homology fully intact while denying that the a.4 label describes the 1ztr coordinates, rejects template use, explains label-structure mismatch for training, recommends filtering on hf, and states required external evidence. Quality metrics used appropriately for representative selection only.

Strong evidence use: fr flag, 50 ATOM vs 99 SEQRES residues, d2hfta2 103 observed residues, Pfam PF00041, species-node siblings (d6r2wt2, d4ylqt2, d3th2t2), FATCAT family statistics, ASTRAL subset files all match the bundle. Reasoning complete: homology unaffected, fragment not a reference, truncated-core scores not comparable, align to full-length TF domain-2 sibling or use SEQRES, complete domains preferred at any identity threshold, AEROSPACI entry-level, SEQRES subsets may still contain fragments, exclude from diversity statistics, no function transfer, release/entry-specific caveat. Noncentral factual error: describes 1o5d as an engineered uPA protease entry; the H/L chain domains (b.47.1.2 plus two g.3.11.1 EGF domains) indicate factor VIIa. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct recommendation (new superfamily in existing fold) with accurate level semantics: family strongest homology claim, superfamily probable ancestry, new fold a structural-novelty claim requiring different topology. Treats placement as a revisable curated hypothesis; lists evidence that would justify merging; states raw superposition scores insufficient; rejects function/template transfer from fold-mates; notes automation only fills existing families. Examples c.1 (sunid 51350) and b.1 (sunid 48725) supported by resolve bundle; release 2.08 / 2.08-2026-08-16 consistent. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct fold d.144/superfamily d.144.1 (56111/56112) and families d.144.1.7 (88854), d.144.1.6 (64411), d.144.1.4 (56171), all bundle-supported; d4ps3a4 and d.15.15 ABD supported. States superfamily implies probable common ancestry and conserved bilobal ATP/Mg phosphotransfer core; explicitly refuses acceptor-substrate and regulation transfer across families, notes pseudokinases and automated matches. Evidence list covers sequence/structural alignment, catalytic and specificity residues, substrate-bound structures, biochemistry, regulation assays, phylogeny/domain architecture. Minor: d.144.1.5 described by its ChaK member rather than the family name 'MHCK/EF2 kinase'; sunid 190091 cited outside bundle but correct. No material errors.
